To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a genome‐wide screen for Wg secretion identifies Emp24 and Ecal, two proteins that act in the early stages of Wg secretion.
Emp24 and its paralog Eca are required for Wg export from the ER.
a genome‐wide screen for regulators of Wg secretion identified two p24 proteins, Emp24 and its homolog Eca, as regulators of ER export of Wg.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms that control the transport and function of Wnt proteins.
the identification of novel components of the Wnt secretion machinery.
the molecular mechanisms of Wnt signalling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors identify two new genes involved in Wnt secretion and propose a model for their function.
the Emp24 and ECA proteins are involved in the ER export of Wingless, but the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
Emp24 and the p24 protein Eca act as cargo receptors to concentrate the Wg cargo in vesicles that bud from the ER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified two novel components of a Wg secretion machinery.
the Wnt/Wg protein is transported from the ER to the Golgi by a specific receptor, and from the Golgi to the plasma membrane by a receptor‐independent pathway.
we have identified two p24 proteins required for Wg export from the ER.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Wnt secretion is a highly regulated process that is not simply a by‐product of the secretory pathway.
Wnt proteins are not secreted by default, and that their secretion requires dedicated machinery.
the secretory pathway of Wnt proteins may be regulated by dedicated factors.
